actions.action: Check soil moisture with finger or chopstick before each watering
Water thoroughly once the top 2-3 cm of soil is dry
Make sure the pot has drainage holes and is not sitting in standing water
Use a chunky well-draining mix of potting soil, perlite and orchid bark
Place in bright indirect light away from AC vents and drafts
Inspect leaf undersides and stem joints for spider mites, wiping with a damp cloth
Trim off the leaf once it is mostly yellow
If more leaves yellow, stems soften or soil smells sour, check roots for rot

reason: The answer leads with transplant stress and lists overwatering/no drainage only as a secondary possibility; the drainage and soil-check advice that would fix it is present but mixed among many other tips, and it includes safeguards, so it is not harmful.
